evidence.clarity: 1440 and 390: H1 'Every truck gets a door and a time.' plus a lede that names the product (dock appointment app), the buyer (mid-size warehouses) and the dispatcher's role; 'Book a demo' sits directly below with '30 minutes, online. Bring your door count and receiving hours.'
evidence.fit: Both audiences have a route: the warehouse gets 'Book a demo' to https://dockline.example/demo in the header, hero and final CTA; dispatchers get 'Carriers: book a slot' to https://book.dockline.example in the nav and footer, plus a line in the final section. Dock vocabulary throughout: dock lights, bumpers, yard clock, hold after start, reefer doors, gate list. At 390 the dispatcher link is only reachable through Menu or far down the page.
evidence.distinctiveness: The hero artifact is an SVG dock face: six numbered doors, red and green dock lights, a yellow edge line, and trailers that back in and out as you drag the 'Yard clock' range input. Below it are a door/hour booking grid and a gate receiving list. Nothing here comes from a template kit.
evidence.proof: 1440: the yard clock, dock face and booking grid are in the first viewport and can be operated. Booking Door 3 10:00 produced a reference (DL-UZFY), an example SMS, a '(yours)' cell, and a trailer at Door 3 once the clock reached 10:00. The gate table (read at 09:30) agrees with the grid: Greenway late at 09:00 and moved to 11:00, Door 3 10:00 open. One inconsistency: the confirmation card books a '53′ dry van' into Door 3, which the rules table lists as 'Reefer'.
evidence.craft: Tokens live on :root (colours, spacing s1–s6, font stacks); the HTML is semantic (header/nav/main/sections with aria-labelledby, table captions, dl). Defects: (1) `.top nav a{color:var(--ink)}` overrides `.btn-primary`, so the header and mobile-menu 'Book a demo' is dark text on green, which axe reports at 3.22:1 at 1440 and is visible in the screenshot; (2) at 390 `.cta-mini + .menu-btn{margin-left:.5rem}` still applies when cta-mini is display:none, so Menu sits beside the logo instead of at the right edge; (3) a 35-character unbroken carrier name puts the confirmation <dd> into the 1fr hero track, which causes 86px of horizontal page overflow at 390. The page is a single 58KB file with system fonts and no network requests. render() rebuilds all 60 cells on every clock input.
evidence.mobile: 390: no overflow in the probe or my tests; text is 13px or larger. The grid becomes one door at a time behind six 44px door tabs; tapping a slot scrolls the form to sheetTop 375 with the Carrier input focused, and the confirmation scrolls into view at the top. The rules table is restacked as label/value rows. Menu opens and closes and closes when a link is followed. The dock illustration and grid start below the first screen.
evidence.honesty: The hero states 'In pilot at two mid-size warehouses we can't name yet, with no measured results to show. The day shown here is a sample you can book into.' The grid ('Sample day with made-up carriers'), the form ('Nothing is sent anywhere'), the gate table caption and the ticket are all labelled where they appear. Minor: '30 minutes, online' and 'Priced per warehouse, by door count' do not come from the brief, and an internal note was left on the page: 'The wording is ours to confirm with the client.'
evidence.interaction: Operated at 1440, 768 and 390. Empty or whitespace-only carrier gives aria-invalid plus 'Enter the carrier name so the gate knows who to expect.' with focus returned. maxlength caps pasted text at 40/24. HTML in inputs is rendered as text (textContent). A passed slot explains itself ('09:00 at Door 3 has passed on the yard clock (09:30)...'). Escape closes the booking sheet and returns focus to the slot. Booking by keyboard (Enter on slot, type, Enter) works. 'Book another hour' with nothing open says so. Reset restores the day and the 09:30 clock. The clock works with arrow keys and End, and an aria-live status reports everything. Gaps: Escape does not close the mobile menu, and about 20 aria-disabled 'Passed' buttons are tab stops. The form accepts Flatbed at reefer Door 3, which contradicts 'only offers doors that take the trailer type'. No console errors.
evidence.copy: Uses the customer's own nouns: 'hold after start', 'Floor-loaded freight adds a second hour', 'Temperature check at the gate', 'It schedules the door, not the warehouse'. Buttons say what they do ('Confirm booking', 'Reset the sample day', 'Book another hour'). Marked down for the leaked 'ours to confirm with the client' note and the dry-van-at-reefer-door example.

evidence.clarity: H1 'Give every truck a door and a time.' with the lede 'Dockline publishes your dock appointment slots. Carriers book a window instead of calling receiving...'. The product is clear. The buyer (warehouse) is implied by 'your' rather than named; 'mid-size warehouses' appears only in the meta description and the footer.
evidence.fit: Both brief URLs are used: 'Book a demo' goes to https://dockline.example/demo, and 'Dispatching a truck? Book an arrival at book.dockline.example' is in the hero at both widths, plus a full dispatcher section. Fit is undercut by claims the brief cannot support (booking speed, setup time, pilot door counts) when the brief says there are no measured results. The dispatcher section is strong.
evidence.distinctiveness: A dark 'Receiving, Building B' Gantt board with a 09:40 now-line, a hazard-striped dock-edge band, the 'One trailer's morning, two ways' timelines, and a laminated-sheet styled rules card. All of it is product-specific.
evidence.proof: The board is operable: picking Door 1 10:00 opens a drawer, and booking returns DL-4482 and a yellow 'mine' block. At 1440 only the board header and the first two rows sit in the first viewport (board top y=675). At 390 the board starts in view, but every open window is scrolled off to the right (board scrollWidth 1080 vs clientWidth 358), so nothing bookable shows without sideways scrolling. Sample data label 'Sample data. Nothing here is a real carrier.' sits in the board foot.
evidence.craft: There is a token sheet (styles.css :root) and separate app.js, but inline styles remain in the HTML (style="margin-top:16px", style="color:#b5c2cc;font-size:14px"). The probe counts 44 text elements under 12px; board labels are 11px and 11.5px and truncated ('KSLR / At ...' under the now-line at 1440). Each 60-minute open window is drawn as a 30-minute-wide button, so the selected highlight covers half the window. makeSlot() builds markup with innerHTML from user input (see interaction). The wordmark links to href="#".
evidence.mobile: 390: no page overflow, but the main artifact is a sideways-scrolling board with a 112px sticky door column. All 16 open windows and the now-line (x=451) start off-screen. Open-window buttons measure 37x42px at 390 and 768, under 44. The nav links are display:none under 720px and there is no menu, so Why, Setup, For dispatchers and Pilots are unreachable from the header (also at 200% zoom). The 'morning' timelines need sideways scroll in non-focusable containers (axe scrollable-region-focusable, 2 nodes) and their text is ellipsis-truncated.
evidence.honesty: Good: the pilots section says the warehouses are unnamed and that there are no numbers yet; the form says 'Nothing you enter leaves this page'. Bad: unsupported performance statements presented as fact: the H2 'Dispatchers book in under a minute', 'the booking takes twenty seconds', 'Setup takes about an hour'. The pilot details 'one with eight doors and one with fourteen' are not in the brief. The 3h35m vs 8 minutes yard-time comparison is an unlabelled illustration that implies savings. 'Tuesday 21 Oct' is a Wednesday in 2026.
evidence.interaction: Clicking an open window opens the drawer and focuses PO. An empty PO sets aria-invalid, and the only message is the placeholder changing to 'Needed: the gate asks for it' (no styling, no aria-describedby). Pallets -5 or 0 are blocked only by the browser's native tooltip. Empty pallets are accepted, although the rules card says the pallet count is required. Empty carrier silently becomes 'Your carrier'. Pasting `` into PO executed the handler (window.__x===1) and logged ERR_FILE_NOT_FOUND, because carrier and PO go into innerHTML. Escape does not close the drawer. 'Close' leaves focus on BODY. There is no reset or undo for bookings. A dry van can be booked on reefer-only Door 5 despite the copy saying it can't.
evidence.copy: Voice is specific and written for the dock: 'your yard stops being a waiting room', 'laminated sheet at the guard shack', 'Late past the grace window and the booking releases; the driver is told to rebook, not to park', 'When a carrier sends a detention invoice, you have the gate stamp'. Marked down for invented numbers stated as fact and for default validation microcopy.
evidence.first_screen: 1440: a specific promise, 'Book a demo', a dispatcher link and the top of the board are in view, but the board rows sit at the very bottom (y≈800+), so the artifact barely makes it in. 390: H1, lede, both CTAs and the dispatcher link are in view, and the board shows only past bookings (06:00–08:00) with no open window.

problems: User input goes into innerHTML in makeSlot(). Pasting `` into the PO field executes script on the page, a pattern that becomes stored XSS once real booking data flows through it.

Unsupported performance claims stated as fact ('Dispatchers book in under a minute', 'the booking takes twenty seconds', 'Setup takes about an hour') when the brief says there are no measured results.

Mobile and keyboard: open windows start off-screen in a sideways-scrolling board, targets are 37x42px, board text is 11px, header nav disappears under 720px with no menu, Escape does not close the drawer, Close drops focus to BODY, and there is no reset.

hard_fail_flags.evidence: The dispatcher section heading presents a booking-speed number as fact: H2#dispatch-title 'Dispatchers book in under a minute. No account.' and .dispatch-foot 'the booking takes twenty seconds'. The setup section adds 'Setup takes about an hour'. The brief says 'we have no measured results yet', and none of these figures come from it. They are not labelled as examples.

Read the H2 'Dispatchers book in under a minute. No account.' and, at the bottom of that section, 'If a carrier books with you every week, they get a saved list of their trucks and the booking takes twenty seconds.' reason: A is the page I would rather maintain. Its demo handles empty, whitespace, long, passed and reset paths, writes all user input with textContent, keeps focus managed through every state, and works one door at a time on a phone with 44px targets. B's board looks good but injects user input as HTML, puts every bookable window off-screen at 390, drops focus on Close, and states unmeasured speed figures as fact. A would need a contrast fix on the nav CTA and the long-name overflow fixed. I would change my mind only if B's injection and mobile board issues were fixed and its numbers removed.
